title: You Know What You Will Like: People Predict Their Own Ratings Better Than Recommender Systems
abstract: arXiv:2611.06696v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recommender systems usually learn what people want from what they have done. Platforms could also ask people directly, but asking is costly: 98.8% of the prompts in our data went unanswered. Theories of statistical prediction imply that a person's own forecast adds little to a recommender algorithm built from many people's behavior. Theories of dispersed knowledge imply that people hold information about their own taste that the data lack. We test the two with the MovieLens Beliefs dataset. In 2023-2024, a homepage prompt asked members how they expected to rate movies they said they had not seen. Of 26,020 such expectations, 551 from 277 members were followed by a rating at least a day later. We compare each expectation with four benchmarks: the platform's own predicted rating, two collaborative-filtering models (matrix factorization and an item neighborhood), and a stack trained on other members' outcomes. translated_title: 你知道自己会喜欢什么：人们对自身评分的预测优于推荐系统
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.06696v1 公告类型：cross 摘要：推荐系统通常从人们已经做过的事情中学习他们想要什么。平台也可以直接询问用户，但询问成本高昂：在我们数据中，98.8%的提问提示无人回应。统计预测理论意味着，个人自身的预测对于基于众多用户行为构建的推荐算法几乎没有额外价值；而分散知识理论则意味着，人们掌握着关于自身品味的、行为数据中所缺失的信息。我们用MovieLens Beliefs数据集对这两种理论进行了检验。在2023至2024年间，主页提示询问成员：他们预期自己会给那些声称尚未看过的电影打多少分。在26,020条此类预期中，有551条（来自277名成员）在至少一天之后伴随着一条实际评分出现。我们将每条预期与四个基准进行比较：平台自身的预测评分、两个协同过滤模型（矩阵分解和物品邻域方法），以及一个在其他成员评分结果上训练的堆叠模型。训练出的模型使用每个……
tldr: 本文利用MovieLens Beliefs数据集实证发现，用户对自己未来电影评分的自我预测优于平台预测及多种协同过滤推荐模型，证明人们掌握着行为数据无法捕捉的关于自身品味的私有信息。
en_tdlr: Using the MovieLens Beliefs dataset, this paper shows that people's own forecasts of their future movie ratings outperform platform predictions and collaborative-filtering models, demonstrating that individuals hold private knowledge of their tastes that behavioral data cannot capture.
